A bound runtime emits its own invocation-class series, named by the runtime ARN, read from the shared causal model's window: throttles are the rejected requests, invocations the admitted ones, system_errors the admitted requests that failed (held-across dependency unavailability and credential failures), total_errors their sum and latency the effective hold. QuotaUnit is the unit the bound quota's demand and limit_rps count, per second: requests, read_units (GetItem) or write_units (PutItem). Required with resource and only with it. Capacity units convert to requests by the operation's own read_units or write_units per request, the AWS provisioned-capacity rule (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/provisioned-capacity-mode.html): one RCU is one strongly consistent read per second, or two eventually consistent reads, of an item up to 4 KB, and one WCU is one write per second of an item up to 1 KB, item sizes rounding up to the next unit. A quota in units is the table capacity the operation draws on, so its limit_rps (with the table's other declared demand) must fit the provisioned capacity.

Resource binds the operation to a declared `quota` resource of the blueprint's causal model (environments[].resources), counted in QuotaUnit. The quota is then the operation's whole arrival declaration: its admitted volume is the successful requests (consuming capacity and observing latency) and its rejected volume the throttled requests (ThrottledRequests, and ReadThrottleEvents for GetItem or WriteThrottleEvents for PutItem), read from the shared model, never re-simulated. A bound operation omits requests_per_second, throttled_requests_per_second and load; read_units or write_units, latency and the latency bounds keep their meaning. Admitted only for GetItem and PutItem, the operations whose throttle families a lab capture observed. One resource binds at most one operation. A table whose GetItem and PutItem operations are all bound is not a table-axis target: quota_reduced on the resource throttles it instead. Omitted keeps the declared-rate behaviour, so default output is unchanged.

ThrottledRequestsPerSecond optionally declares requests of this operation rejected for exceeding provisioned throughput, an explicit operator assumption (omitted or zero: no throttling and no throttle series). Throttled requests are separate from requests_per_second: they consume no capacity and have no latency or returned items. Admitted only for GetItem and PutItem, the operations a lab capture of a provisioned table observed. Each throttled request is one sample of 1 in ThrottledRequests (TableName+Operation) and in ReadThrottleEvents (GetItem) or WriteThrottleEvents (PutItem) on TableName; unthrottled requests add no zero samples. Follows the operation's load.

DurationLoad selects whether duration_ms_idle follows the business curve without the arrival rates doing so. Empty or "constant" leaves the duration switch to `load: business`. "business" makes the mean duration follow the curve (as duration_ms_idle describes) while the four arrival rates stay at their configured constants, which models a scheduled function that fires at a fixed cadence but does less work per run off-peak. It requires duration_ms_idle and is valid with any `load`; with `load: business` it changes nothing. Operator assumption, not an AWS behaviour.

DurationMSIdle opts the function into load-following batch duration: with `load: business`, the mean per-execution duration moves with the business curve from this idle (curve value 0) duration up to duration_ms (curve value 1.0, the weekday business-hours plateau), so a scheduled batch does less work per run overnight and on weekends. The curve factor is capped at 1, so duration_ms stays the ceiling. duration_ms_min/duration_ms_max, when declared, scale with the mean so they keep bracketing it. Positive and not above duration_ms, and only valid with `load: business` or `duration_load: business`. Zero (omitted) keeps the constant duration, so default output is unchanged. Operator assumption, not an AWS behaviour.
DurationMSMax is the upper bound of the per-execution duration distribution, in milliseconds, with the same rules as duration_ms_min. It must not be below duration_ms.

DurationMSMin is the lower bound of the per-execution duration distribution, in milliseconds. duration_ms stays the mean (Duration _sum and _average unchanged). Must be declared together with duration_ms_max (both zero means constant duration) and not exceed duration_ms. The observed Minimum moves from the mean toward this bound as executions per window increase and is limited so a sample set with the window's sum exists; one execution has no spread. A bound equal to duration_ms leaves no room for spread on either side.

Load selects how the arrival rates follow time. Empty or "constant" keeps every rate fixed (the default). "business" scales invocations_per_min, async_received_per_min, stream_batches_per_min and throttles_per_min together by the blueprint's business curve (diurnal x weekly x master volume), so the disjoint populations stay coherent and error_fraction applies to the scaled executions. The configured rates are then the rate at a curve value of 1.0 (weekday business-hours plateau). Operator assumption, not an AWS behaviour.

Resource binds the function to a declared `concurrency` resource of the blueprint's causal model (environments[].resources). The resource is then the function's whole declaration: Throttles are the window's rejected requests, Invocations the admitted ones, Errors the admitted executions that failed (held-across dependency unavailability and credential failures, plus the optional error_fraction background share below), ConcurrentExecutions the in-use concurrency and Duration the effective hold. They are read from the shared model, never re-simulated. A bound function omits every arrival-rate and duration field (invocations_per_min, async_received_per_min, async_dropped_fraction, async_age_ms, stream_batches_per_min, iterator_age_ms, throttles_per_min, duration_ms, duration_ms_min, duration_ms_max, duration_ms_idle, duration_load, load) except error_fraction, which a bound function may declare as a background share of its admitted invocations that fail regardless of faults (an operator assumption for the captured baseline; the model fails work only through faults). Errors are that share of the admitted executions plus the model's failures, never more than the admitted executions, selected by the same fractional carry as an unbound function (deterministic, no random draw). A bound function is not a target of the function-axis modes; incidents reach it through the resource-axis modes (concurrency_reduced, dependency_slow, dependency_unavailable, credential_expired). One resource binds at most one function. Omitted keeps the function-axis behaviour, so default output is unchanged.

ZeroValuedSamples makes Throttles and Errors observe every request (execution attempts plus throttled requests) with 1 for the event and 0 otherwise, as a lab capture of this service reported, instead of only the events. Throttles then has Sum = throttles and SampleCount = requests; Errors has Sum = errors and the same SampleCount, throttled requests contributing 0. A window with no request still emits neither. Omitted keeps the event-only observations, so default output is unchanged.

Burst, when declared, concentrates the queue's arrivals into the on-fraction of each period instead of spreading them evenly, as an upstream batch pipeline delivers: the same mean volume (arrivals_per_second, scaled by load when that is business) arrives in the first duty x period of each period, offset by phase, and nothing arrives in the rest. Periods are aligned to the Unix epoch on the tick wall clock, so the on-window needs no state and a restart or a master pause resumes on the same schedule. Receives are unchanged, so a backlog forms during a burst while arrivals exceed receives_per_second and drains afterwards. Omitted (the default) leaves arrivals evenly spread. A queue bound to a resource rejects it.

Enrichment selects only the P2 key vocabulary. All values are declared; omitted keys stay absent. P1/P3 tag alternatives cannot be union-filled.

Load selects how the queue's traffic follows the blueprint's business curve. Empty (the default) keeps arrivals_per_second and receives_per_second constant. "business" treats arrivals_per_second as the peak-plateau arrival rate and scales it each second by the shape engine's business factor (diurnal x weekly x volume). Consumers then take what is visible, one message per receive, but never faster than receives_per_second, which becomes the maximum consumer throughput: a backlog forms only while scaled arrivals exceed it and drains once they fall back. Receives follow arrivals, so idle consumers add no empty-receive polling. Without a shape engine the factor is 1.

Resource binds the queue to a declared `queue` resource (environments[].resources).
